item.title: Wakayama's Marine Museums and Aquariums: Life of the Kuroshio — Guide
item.description: The Kii Peninsula’s coast is washed by the warm Kuroshio current, which carries subtropical marine life far north and makes Wakayama’s waters some of the richest in Japan — home to coral, sea turtles and an enormous variety of fish. The prefecture’s marine museums and aquariums showcase this abundance, with displays on the Kuroshio ecosystem, coral communities and the loggerhead sea turtles that nest on local beaches, alongside touch pools and conservation exhibits.
